name: Pelargonic acid

pubchem.title: Nonanoic Acid
pubchem.description: Nonanoic acid is a C9 straight-chain saturated fatty acid which occurs naturally as esters of the oil of pelargonium. Has antifungal properties, and is also used as a herbicide as well as in the preparation of plasticisers and lacquers. It has a role as an antifeedant, a plant metabolite, a Daphnia magna metabolite and an algal metabolite. It is a straight-chain saturated fatty acid and a medium-chain fatty acid. It is a conjugate acid of a nonanoate. It derives from a hydride of a nonane.

consumer_summary.what_it_is: Pelargonic acid, also known as nonanoic acid, is a medium-chain fatty acid that occurs naturally in the essential oils of pelargoniums. In daily life, you might encounter it as a natural herbicide used in gardening, or as a building block in the manufacturing of lacquers and plastics. It is also recognized for its natural antifungal and insect-deterring properties.
consumer_summary.found_in: This fatty acid is found in familiar botanicals like licorice root (Glycyrrhiza glabra), marshmallow plant (Althaea officinalis), and arnica (Arnica montana).
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are drawn to pelargonic acid for its dual nature as both a potent botanical defense compound and a biomarker in human metabolism. With over 200 published papers, scientists are actively exploring its antimicrobial properties and its effects on the skin. The strongest evidence so far comes from individual randomised trials (Oxford level 1b) investigating its antimicrobial potential.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether pelargonic acid can effectively inhibit bacterial or fungal growth in clinical settings.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A larger, multi-center randomized controlled trial evaluating topical pelargonic acid against standard treatments for specific fungal or bacterial skin infections over several weeks.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Early animal work points toward a potential to modulate inflammatory pathways, and researchers want to know if this translates to human health.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A first-in-human safety and biomarker study measuring systemic inflammatory markers in healthy volunteers taking a controlled oral dose over two weeks.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: If this bears out, pelargonic acid could serve as a natural, plant-derived alternative to synthetic insect repellents.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A human volunteer study testing the efficacy and duration of a pelargonic acid topical formulation against mosquito landings compared to a standard DEET control.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are investigating whether circulating levels of this fatty acid are linked to sleep quality or sedative states.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, placebo-controlled trial measuring sleep architecture via polysomnography in adults given a pelargonic acid supplement before bed.

consumer_summary.cautions: Because it is used industrially as a herbicide and is a known skin irritant at high concentrations, concentrated pelargonic acid should be handled with care and not applied directly to the skin without proper dilution.
consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: Best evidence so far is an individual randomised trial (Oxford level 1b) for its antimicrobial properties, while most other health claims rest on animal and observational research.
